_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 50 (Jacob's burial; Joseph reassures brothers; Joseph's death). Saadia-specific: v.2 'אלאטבא' = 'the physicians' for רפאים — Saadia gives the Egyptian embalmers their professional designation; v.10 'אנדר אלעוסג' = 'threshing-floor of the bramble' for גרן האטד; v.20 'אנתם קדרתם עלי שרא ואללה קדר כ'ירא' = 'you intended for me evil but God intended good' (Saadia's gloss for חשבתם — substitutes 'intended/decreed' for 'thought').

translations.1: And Joseph fell upon the face of his father, and wept over him, and kissed him.
translations.2: And he commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.
translations.3: Until forty days were completed for him — for thus were the days of those embalmed completed. And the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.
translations.4: And when the days of his mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's house, saying: 'If I have found favor with you, speak to Pharaoh, and say to him:
translations.5: "My father made me swear, saying: 'Behold, I am dying; bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan.' Now — let me go up and bury my father, and I shall return."'
translations.6: Pharaoh said: 'Go up — bury your father, as he made you swear.'
translations.7: And Joseph went up to bury his father; and there went up with him all the officers of Pharaoh, and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt.
translations.8: And all the household of Joseph, and his brothers, and the household of his father — except for their little ones, and their sheep and cattle, which they left in the land of al-Sadir (Goshen).
translations.9: And there went up with him chariots and horsemen; and the camp was very great.
translations.10: And they came to the threshing-floor of the bramble — which is across the Jordan; and they lamented there a very great lamentation; and he made for his father a mourning of seven days.
translations.11: And the Canaanite dweller of the land saw the mourning at the threshing-floor of the bramble; and they said: 'This is a heavy mourning for the Egyptians.' Therefore it was named Mourning of the Egyptians — which is across the Jordan.
translations.12: And his sons did for him according to all that he had commanded them.
translations.13: And his sons carried him to the land of Canaan; and they buried him in the cave of the doubled field, which Abraham bought as a burial-place from Ephron the Hittite, over against Mamre.
translations.14: Then Joseph returned to Egypt — he and his brothers, and the rest of those who had gone up with him to bury his father — after he had buried him.
translations.15: And when Joseph's brothers saw that their father had died, they said: 'Lest Joseph threaten us, and repay us for the evil which we had done to him.'
translations.16: And they commanded one to say to Joseph: 'Your father commanded us before his death, saying:
translations.17: "Thus shall you say to Joseph: O Joseph, forgive the sin of your brothers, and their offense — for they did evil to you. And now, we ask you to pardon the offense of the servants of the God of your father."' And Joseph wept when they spoke to him so.
translations.18: And his brothers also went, and fell down before him, and said: 'Behold, we are slaves to you.'
translations.19: Joseph said to them: 'Do not fear — for I fear God.
translations.20: You intended evil against me; but God intended good — that He might do as you see this day, to keep many people alive.
translations.21: And now — do not fear. I shall sustain you and your little ones.' And he consoled them, and spoke kindly with them.
translations.22: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt — he and his father's household. And he lived a hundred and ten years.
translations.23: And he saw to Ephraim sons of the third generation; and also the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born upon his knees.
translations.24: And Joseph said to his brothers: 'I am dying; and God shall surely remember you, and bring you up from this land — to the land which God promised to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.'
translations.25: And Joseph made the children of Israel swear, saying: 'When God remembers you, you shall bring up my bones from here.'
translations.26: And Joseph died, a son of a hundred and ten years; and they embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
